concepts.def: The 1920s economic boom in the USA marked by mass production, consumer credit, rising share prices and cultural change before the crash.
The sudden collapse of US stock prices in October 1929, wiping out fortunes and triggering the worldwide Great Depression.
The severe economic slump of the 1930s bringing mass unemployment, bank failures and poverty across the United States.
President Hoover's belief in limited government intervention, blamed for failing to relieve Depression suffering and his 1932 election defeat.
Franklin Roosevelt's programme of relief, recovery and reform from 1933, using federal agencies and public works to combat the Depression.
The boost to US industry and employment from Second World War production, which finally ended the Depression and revived the economy.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The USA c1920-55: Boom, Bust & Recovery — a core area of A-Level History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The USA c1920-55: Boom, Bust & Recovery brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The USA c1920-55: Boom, Bust & Recovery.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What name is given to the US economic boom of the 1920s?
options: The Roaring Twenties
The New Deal
The Great Society
The Square Deal

mcqs.q: What event in October 1929 triggered the Great Depression?
options: The Wall Street Crash
Pearl Harbor
Prohibition
The New Deal

mcqs.q: Who introduced the New Deal to fight the Depression?
options: Franklin Roosevelt
Herbert Hoover
Woodrow Wilson
Harry Truman

mcqs.q: What finally ended the Great Depression in the USA?
options: Wartime industrial production
The Wall Street Crash
Prohibition
Hoover's policies

mcqs.q: Did the New Deal end the Great Depression?
options: The New Deal caused the Wall Street Crash.
It eased suffering and reduced unemployment but did not fully cure the economy; recovery came mainly with wartime production after 1941.
The New Deal completely ended the Depression by itself.
Hoover was a socialist who nationalised industry.

mcqs.q: Why did the 1920s boom collapse in 1929?
options: The boom collapsed because of the Second World War.
The crash happened because Roosevelt was elected.
Hoover was a socialist who nationalised industry.
Overproduction, speculation, unequal wealth and risky credit made the stock market unstable, leading to the Wall Street Crash.

mcqs.q: How did Hoover respond to the Depression?
options: The New Deal caused the Wall Street Crash.
Hoover launched the New Deal to fight the Depression.
Hoover favoured limited intervention and self-help, which proved inadequate, contributing to his defeat by Roosevelt in 1932.
Hoover was a socialist who nationalised industry.
